limited_overlap.description: 86 of 1500 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 83,270 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
116 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 1277 of 1500 applicants answered (85.1%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.31 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Effect-modifier claims were not computed because the chosen final model is not linear.
Final model: causal_forest. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0268, causal_forest=0.0013.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -1.9; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = -0.54. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 23010 (90% -103505 to 149525).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 6114 (90% 2951 to 9278); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -1918, without months_unemployed = 4638, without education = 5057; full model = 4581.
Run time 6 seconds with seed 1; training rows 1500, responders 1277.
